from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

bg = load_bg()
feats = ["log_walk_l2", "l2_ports_800", "drive_dcfc_min", "garage_share", "attached_share", "med_income"]
bg["log_walk_l2"] = np.log1p(bg.walk_l2_m)
X_df = bg.dropna(subset=feats).copy()
X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X_df[feats])
print(f"Block groups clustered: {len(X_df)}")


Block groups clustered: 1229




Code
ks = range(2, 10)
inertia, sil = [], []
for k in ks:
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=20, random_state=42).fit(X)
    inertia.append(km.inertia_); sil.append(silhouette_score(X, km.labels_))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
ax[0].plot(ks, inertia, marker="o"); ax[0].set_title("Inertia"); ax[0].set_xlabel("k")
ax[1].plot(ks, sil, marker="o"); ax[1].set_title("Silhouette"); ax[1].set_xlabel("k")
from kneed import KneeLocator
print("Elbow k:", KneeLocator(list(ks), inertia, curve="convex", direction="decreasing").knee)


Elbow k: 4











Code
# Silhouette is highest at k=2 (0.39) but two groups are too coarse to describe.
# Among k >= 3, k=5 has the highest silhouette (0.27) and separates the

title: Plugged In or Left Out?
text:
Approach

Station inventory: Alternative Fuel Stations API, public and operating, city plus a one-mile buffer
Neighborhood data: ACS 2023 five-year (tract income, block group housing type) and OPA garage records
Network distances with OSMnx: walk to Level 2, drive to DC fast
Group comparisons by income, garage share, and housing type; K-means profiles of limited access

title: Plugged In or Left Out?
text:
Key findings
Results cover 1,246 block groups with housing units, 195 public Level 2 stations, and 28 DC fast stations within one mile of the city.

Most residents are not within walking distance of public Level 2 charging. The median walk from a block group to the nearest station is 1.97 km. In 61% of block groups the walk is more than a mile, and only 18.5% have any Level 2 port within 800 m.
Among block groups where few homes have a garage, lower-income areas are farther from charging. These are the residents who most depend on public chargers. Lower-income block groups in this group have a median walk of 1,853 m, compared with 1,083 m in higher-income ones. Only 17% have a port within 800 m, compared with 38%. Their median drive to DC fast charging is also longer: 4.1 minutes compared with 2.3 (all differences p < 0.001).
Attached housing compounds the gap. In lower-income block groups where most units are single-family attached, only 3% have a Level 2 port within 800 m.
Stations in higher-income tracts tend to have opened earlier. Among operating stations inside the city, the median recorded opening date is July 2023 in higher-income tracts and November 2023 in lower-income tracts (p = 0.009). Every station has a recorded opening date. Closed stations are not in the inventory.
One access profile stands out. K-means identifies 434 block groups with about 224,000 housing units where almost no homes have a garage, 77% of units are attached, a median 35% of households have no vehicle, and the median walk to Level 2 charging is 2 km. Median tract income in this group is $40,600, the lowest of the five profiles.


Limitations

The station inventory lists only operating stations, so opening dates describe today’s network, not its full history.
Garage records miss driveways without a garage, so off-street parking is understated.
Income is measured at the tract level and assigned to each block group; 17 block groups lack a tract income estimate.
Distances are measured from block group centroids, not from individual homes.
